findings.reason: an implementer following §2 literally joins on the worker harness session, so the fixture's stated sessions (cdb769a4, 83d14db1, e1b445e1) resolve to the wrong rows, or the test is built against the wrong field and passes while the board labels runs with the worker's session.
findings.text: §2 declares "A plan's coordinator is the `session_id` of its most recent dispatched run", but the ledger's `session_id` is the worker's own harness session and the coordinator is the dispatching crew session, held in the separate `session` field (`reckon/ledger.py:162-165` and `reckon/run_record.py:538-539`: "The crew session that dispatched the run, distinct from `session_id` (the worker's own harness session)"). §2's own cited artefacts contradict it: `_live_review_runs` (`reckon/crew/obligations.py:430`) filters pointers on `pointer.get("session")`, which §2 describes as "filters runs by the dispatching session", and `reckon/crew/directory.py:146-157` groups coordinator rows by `record.get("session")` — the field §5 says resolves the coordinator's peer name

findings.reason: §1's whole motivation is reads refused at the 80,000-character MCP ceiling and §8 measures the new reads against that ceiling, so boundedness is load-bearing; the plan must either state that paging is added to the directory view or drop the bound rather than assert a paging capability the cited view does not have.
findings.text: §5's done-when requires the board to "stay bounded at workstation scope through its paging", and §5's mechanism fixes the interface budget as "no crew view is added; directory gains fields" — but `crew(view="directory")` has no paging to page with: `reckon/mcp_views.py:3805-3813` returns `crew_directory(project, run_id=..., node_id=...)` early, passing neither `limit` nor `cursor`, and `reckon/crew/directory.py` carries no limit/cursor handling. §3's parallel claim that the ready-idle read "pages with the view's own paging" rests on the same gap, since `ready_set_view` (`reckon/mcp_views.py:1128) takes no cursor or limit and returns every ready row

findings.reason: the decision sanctions a new crew view and the sections forbid one, so an implementer must guess which governs; the decision rationale is a leftover of the pre-change design and needs rewording to match the extended-directory and extended-lanes design the sections now describe.
findings.text: the `board-surface` decision's rationale records that the board (§5) and the lane share (§6) "are one new bounded crew view joining directory, scopes, live and lanes", while the §5 the change produced states "Interface budget: no crew view is added; directory gains fields" and §6 states "no view is added"

findings.reason: the file and module resolve and any implementer reads the lane parser there regardless, so the stale line number costs a lookup but does not change what a node builds.
findings.text: §6 cites "The document is parsed once, in `reckon/crew/lane_document.py:447`", but line 447 is `read_lane_admission`, a downstream reader of an already-parsed document, while the parser is `read_lane_document` at `reckon/crew/lane_document.py:303`

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — §6's parser anchor points at the wrong function in a file that otherwise resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §5's done-when makes the board's boundedness rest on paging (`stays bounded at workstation scope through its paging`) that the `directory` view it extends does not have.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — s2–s6 require no session-scratch path; their fixtures are the committed power_convertor ledger at 2026-10-22T08:50Z and the gate logs stay on the node that runs them.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or version tags appear in any symbol or comment introduced by s2–s6.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §2 derives the coordinator from the ledger's `session_id`, but that field is the worker's harness session; the dispatching crew session is the ledger's separate `session` field, which the plan's own cited artefacts key on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of s2–s6 names one deliverable (the coordinator resolver, the extended ready-set view, the critical-path state fields, the extended directory, the extended lanes view).
